title: The Value of Small Good Deeds
summary: Small acts of kindness are valuable and rewarded.
translation: Whether big or small, it is not necessary to perform a grand deed for it to be accepted as good. Even a minor good deed is accepted by Allah and adds weight to our record of deeds. That is why the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) outlined in various hadiths that small acts can also be virtuous. For example, saying 'Subhan Allah' or 'Allahu Akbar' even once is charity and is a form of good deed. Just like giving money in charity brings rewards, uttering these words also earns the reward of charity. In one hadith, narrated in Sahih Muslim and by Hazrat Abdul Razi Allah's pleasure be upon him, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.' This means even simply smiling when meeting someone, whether a friend or an enemy, brings reward. Therefore, no good deed should be considered insignificant. This hadith emphasizes that any good deed, even if small, should be performed as it could be accepted by Allah. Maulana Idrees Sahib Kandhalvi (may Allah have mercy upon him) states that meeting someone with a smiling face is a good deed because it brings joy and happiness to others, fostering love, which is a beloved action. Thus, some scholars say even when meeting an enemy, one should meet with a cheerful demeanor. There is a narration that Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, 'The Prophet (peace be upon him) was sitting among us speaking negatively about someone. After a while, the same person arrived, and the Prophet warmly greeted him.' This shows the importance of meeting everyone, even adversaries, with a smiling face, as it earns respect and happiness from others.
